title: WebSocket
subtitle: One authenticated WebSocket per call carries the binary audio link between Teams and my voice engine, and survives a mid-call reconnect.

stats.label: audio pacing the media SDK expects
soak with a forced mid-call reconnect

lede: Helix answers Microsoft Teams calls with a voice engine on my own GPUs under Linux, and Teams hands raw call audio only to a Windows application built on Microsoft's real-time media SDK. I kept all intelligence on my side and made the Windows piece a media driver, joined to the engine by a WebSocket link carrying a binary media protocol I designed. Each call gets one authenticated, full-duplex secure WebSocket between the bridge and the engine, so a call's lifetime equals its socket's. On the Linux side an Axum endpoint admits a session only when its tenant, persona and identity fingerprint match what the engine expects.
quote: I can design a real-time protocol across two languages, two clouds and a vendor SDK with strict rules, and prove it under soak and fault before I call it finished.
evidence: Microsoft Teams real-time media: one authenticated full-duplex WebSocket per call between a .NET media bridge and a Rust voice engine, admitted by tenant, persona and fingerprint.
Binary protocol design: 2 implementations, C# and Rust, held to byte-identical output with shared golden vectors, audio paced at 20 ms.
Fault tolerance in real-time systems: a 30 min soak and a forced reconnect inside the same call, with audio from the gap dropped.
author: Corey James
